title: KardioKompetent study – mHealth intervention to improve eHealth literacy in patients with heart failure and/or coronary heart disease
summary:
Background
Cardiovascular diseases such as heart failure and coronary heart disease are among the most common conditions worldwide. Health information from the internet is playing an increasingly important role in managing such conditions. However, many people find it difficult to search for specific online information on health topics, assess its quality, and apply what they read in a meaningful way to their own health. This ability is referred to as “eHealth literacy.” Studies show that a large portion of the German population needs support in this area—especially people with chronic conditions.

Research Question
The study investigates whether a digital training program called “KardioKompetent” can improve the ehealth literacy of patients with heart disease. In addition, the study examines whether using the app also improves quality of life, health behaviors, and confidence in one’s own ability to manage the condition.

Methodology
The study includes 192 patients with heart failure and/or coronary heart disease. Participants are randomly assigned to two groups: one group receives access to the “KardioKompetent” app, while the other does not. The app contains seven main modules and six exercise modules, which are unlocked alternately every three days. The time required to complete the modules is approximately 15–20 minutes per week. The content provides knowledge and practical exercises related to searching for, finding, understanding, evaluating, and applying health information on the internet—presented in the form of videos, audio files, and interactive tasks. The training lasts a total of 37 days. All participants complete online questionnaires at several points in time: before the start of the training, upon completion, and one and three months later. This allows researchers to observe whether and how long any improvements last. The group without app access will also have the opportunity to use the training after the study ends.

interventions.name: Arm 1: Intervention group—mHealth intervention using KardioKompetent, alternating between information and exercise modules on eHealth literacy every three days, for 37 days

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Diagnosed heart failure and/or coronary heart disease
• Proficiency in German
• Internet-enabled smartphone
• Electronic informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
• Physical, neurological, and cognitive limitations that prevent
participation in the intervention
• No private internet access
